title: Schedule II Prescriptions, Emergency Oral Orders, and Partial Fills
learning_objectives: Distinguish a prohibited refill from a lawful remainder of a partial fill.
Choose the correct deadline by identifying why and under which pathway a Schedule II prescription was partially filled.
Apply the emergency oral quantity and follow-up requirements as separate conditions.

quick_review.text: A Schedule II prescription may not be refilled; a lawful unfilled remainder is not a refill.

Emergency oral Schedule II dispensing is limited to the amount adequate to treat the patient during the emergency period, and the pharmacist must make a reasonable effort to confirm the oral authorization came from a registered practitioner if that practitioner is not known to the pharmacist.
The prescriber must deliver the required written or electronic follow-up prescription within seven days after authorizing the emergency oral dispensing.
If that emergency oral follow-up does not arrive within seven days, the pharmacist must notify the DEA.
A Schedule II prescription for an LTCF resident or terminally ill patient has a separate partial-fill pathway lasting up to 60 days from issue unless discontinued sooner.
A Massachusetts written or electronic Schedule II prescription becomes invalid 30 days after issue.

decision_logic.condition: The original Schedule II quantity was fully dispensed.
decision_logic.action: Do not process an additional dispensing as a refill; require a new lawful prescription unless another distinct pathway applies.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacy could not supply the full Schedule II quantity.
decision_logic.action: Use the federal stock-shortage partial-fill pathway and its 72-hour remainder rule.

decision_logic.condition: The patient or prescriber requested a partial fill of a non-emergency written or electronic Schedule II prescription and State law does not prohibit it.
decision_logic.action: Use the request-based pathway and complete any remainder no later than 30 days after the prescription was written, while also satisfying Massachusetts conditions.

decision_logic.condition: The patient or prescriber requests a partial fill of an emergency oral Schedule II prescription.
decision_logic.action: Use the request-based emergency exception and complete any remainder no later than 72 hours after the prescription was issued.

decision_logic.condition: The Schedule II prescription is for an LTCF resident or a terminally ill patient.
decision_logic.action: Use the special federal documentation pathway; partial fillings may continue for no more than 60 days from issue and must stop sooner if the prescription is discontinued.

decision_logic.condition: The emergency oral Schedule II follow-up has not reached the pharmacy within seven days after oral authorization.
decision_logic.action: The pharmacist must notify the DEA of the practitioner's failure to deliver the required follow-up prescription.

decision_logic.condition: A Massachusetts patient requests a lesser quantity.
decision_logic.action: Record the partial fill, keep later remainder dispensing at the same pharmacy, and apply the Massachusetts issue-date deadlines.

ma_vs_federal.text: Federal patient-requested partial filling is permissive and requires only that the partial fill not be prohibited by State law; Massachusetts goes further and makes the lesser-quantity dispensing mandatory on patient request while adding same-pharmacy, patient-record, and issue-date conditions.

exceptions.text: The 72-hour remainder rule is tied to the pharmacy's inability to supply the full quantity and should not be substituted for a patient-requested partial-fill pathway.
The request-based 30-day remainder rule has a separate emergency-oral exception: an emergency oral Schedule II remainder must be completed within 72 hours after issue.
Do not apply the ordinary 30-day request-based deadline to the special LTCF or terminal-illness pathway, which may continue for up to 60 days from issue unless discontinued sooner.

Massachusetts' five-day initial partial-dispensing limit in this statute applies to prescriptions filled under the specified out-of-state Schedule II subsections, not every patient-requested partial fill.

timing_deadlines.consequence: The required written or electronic follow-up must reach the pharmacy.

timing_deadlines.event: Missing emergency oral Schedule II follow-up
timing_deadlines.consequence: The pharmacist must notify the DEA of the practitioner's failure to deliver the follow-up prescription.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 72 hours of the first partial filling
timing_deadlines.consequence: Otherwise notify the prescriber and obtain a new prescription for further quantity.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: No later than 30 days after issue
timing_deadlines.consequence: For a non-emergency written or electronic prescription, the remaining portion cannot be dispensed after the deadline.

timing_deadlines.event: Request-based emergency oral Schedule II remainder
timing_deadlines.timeframe: No later than 72 hours after issue
timing_deadlines.consequence: The emergency oral remainder cannot use the ordinary 30-day request-based period.

timing_deadlines.event: LTCF or terminal-illness Schedule II partial fills
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Up to 60 days from issue unless discontinued sooner
timing_deadlines.consequence: Further partial dispensing must stop at the 60-day limit or upon earlier discontinuation.

timing_deadlines.event: Massachusetts written or electronic Schedule II validity

forms_records.text: Massachusetts requires a notation of each partial dispensing and quantity in the pharmacy patient record, accessible to the prescriber on request.
LTCF and terminal-illness Schedule II partial fills must use the special federal documentation framework for that pathway.
A Massachusetts prescription for a Schedule II opioid must itself carry a notation that the patient may fill it, upon request, in an amount not exceeding the full prescribed quantity.

role_duties.duty: Identify the factual trigger for a partial fill before selecting a deadline.
Deliver the required emergency oral Schedule II follow-up prescription within seven days.
Notify the DEA if the practitioner fails to deliver the emergency oral Schedule II follow-up within seven days.
Dispense the lesser quantity when a Massachusetts patient requests a partial fill of a Schedule II prescription; that dispensing is mandatory rather than discretionary.

common_traps.text: Calling every later Schedule II dispensing a refill erases the lawful partial-fill remainder distinction.
Choosing 72 hours whenever a Schedule II prescription is partial ignores who requested the partial fill and why.
Applying 30 days to every request-based remainder misses the 72-hour emergency-oral exception and the separate 60-day LTCF or terminal-illness path.
Reading the Massachusetts patient-requested partial fill as an option the pharmacist may decline turns a mandatory duty into a permission.
